US-119-S5628.description: A bill to amend the Consumer Financial Protection Act of 2010 to enhance rule-making requirements for the Bureau of Consumer Financial Protection, and for other purposes.
US-119-S5628.aiSummary: The bill would add new steps the Consumer Financial Protection Bureau must follow when it proposes a rule. It would require the bureau to explain why the rule is needed, review costs and benefits, look at other options, and say how the rule might affect small businesses, consumers, and state, local, and tribal governments. It would also require the bureau to include the assumptions, studies, and data behind its analysis.

US-119-S2658.title: Medication Affordability and Patent Integrity Act
US-119-S2658.summary:
Medication Affordability and Patent Integrity Act

This bill requires applicants seeking approval of a drug or licensure of a biological product to submit certain information about relevant patents to both the Food and Drug Administration (FDA) and the U.S. Patent and Trademark Office (USPTO).

Specifically, the bill requires applicants to make certifications and disclosures related to each applicable patent on a proposed drug or biological product. An applicable patent is a patent or patent application held or sought by the applicant for the drug or biological product (including a formulation or composition, method of use, or method of manufacturing).

For each applicable patent, an applicant must submit to the USPTO any information material to patentability that the applicant submitted to the FDA and any information provided by the FDA in response. The applicant must certify that this submission is complete and consistent with the information the applicant provided to the FDA.

Further, for each applicable patent, an applicant must certify that certain information submitted to the FDA is consistent with information the applicant provided to the USPTO. This is specific to statements or characterizations that are material to patentability and related to (1) an applicable patent (including a statement or characterization of relevant publicly known information), or (2) analytical data included in a new drug or biological product application.

The bill establishes a defense to a patent infringement action if the owner of an applicable patent negligently or intentionally failed to make the disclosures required by these provisions.

US-119-HR3937.title: Wabeno Economic Development Act
US-119-HR3937.summary:
Wabeno Economic Development Act

This bill requires the Forest Service to convey approximately 14 acres of federal land, including the mineral rights, in the Chequamegon-Nicolet National Forest, Wisconsin, to Tony's Wabeno Redi-Mix, LLC, upon receiving an offer to buy the land for market value.

The Forest Service must complete an appraisal to determine the market value of the land, and the offer must be received within 180 days after federal approval of such appraisal. Tony's Wabeno Redi-Mix, LLC, must pay an amount equal to the market value of the land and all associated costs as a condition of conveyance.

Additionally, the Department of the Interior must publish a comprehensive review of the federal permitting processes for the development of stone, sand, and gravel on federal lands.

Introduced in Senate

US-119-S4715.description: A bill to amend the Outer Continental Shelf Lands Act to establish fitness to operate standards and decommissioning escrow accounts for offshore oil and gas operators, and for other purposes.
US-119-S4715.aiSummary: The bill would set fitness-to-operate rules for offshore oil and gas operators on the outer continental shelf. Before a lease, easement, or right-of-way could be issued, extended, or transferred, the company would have to meet standards tied to past law compliance, financial strength, safety, and cleanup duties. It would also require decommissioning escrow accounts and direct the Interior Department to review compliance each year and report to Congress.

US-119-S4979.aiSummary: The bill would set up a process to help keep the Social Security trust funds financially stable over the long term. It would have the Social Security Advisory Board gather public input, hold listening sessions, and send Congress a report with recommendations and draft bill language. It would also set deadlines for Congress to take up that language and for committees in both chambers to review it.

US-119-S2878.title: Great Lakes Fishery Research Reauthorization Act
US-119-S2878.summary:
Great Lakes Fishery Research Reauthorization Act

This act reauthorizes through FY2030 research and monitoring conducted by the U.S. Geological Survey in support of binational fisheries within the Great Lakes Basin. This research is completed through the Great Lakes Science Center and may involve invasive species science, studies on fishery resources, and the use of biological assessment tools and other capabilities to support fishery management decisions.
